$comment: The rink as coordinates, and the corpus's position vocabulary expressed against it.
OWNERSHIP. Every dimension here is owned by content/foundation/rink_map.md.
This file does not get to disagree with it: scripts/check_geometry.py reads the numbers
out of that document and fails if they diverge. If a dimension is wrong, fix the owner
first and this file second — never the other way round.
COORDINATES. Origin at centre ice. x runs along the length, -100 to +100 (200 ft).
y runs across the width, -42.5 to +42.5 (85 ft). Positive x is the attacking end when a
diagram is drawn left-to-right; positive y is the side the diagram calls 'right'.
Units are feet throughout, because that is the unit the owning document leads with.
WHY NAMED POSITIONS. A diagram source should read like the corpus, not like a drawing
program: 'half-wall-right', not '[69, 36]'. The named table is also the single place the
corpus's spatial vocabulary is defined, which is what stops 'the wall' meaning two things.
Anything relational rather than positional — 'quiet ice', 'the house', 'behind the wall'
in its defensive-line sense — is deliberately absent. Those are not points on a rink.

faceoff.$neutral_dot_note: OUTSIDE the blue line, i.e. in the NEUTRAL zone. The owner says '5 ft outside your own blue line'. This was 30 — five feet the wrong way, putting all four dots inside the end zones on every diagram the corpus draws. check_geometry asserted |blue_line_x +/- 5| and so never saw the sign.

trapezoid.$comment: Rule 1.8 figures. NEVER take these from Rule 27.8, which is stale pre-2014 wording — the owning document flags the divergence in four places, one of them a blockquote of its own (§3 "Two rules, two different numbers"), the others a sentence in its IIHF note, a Key Takeaway and its verification trailer. (This note used to say "four paragraphs on why"; only the blockquote is a paragraph on why.)

positions.$comment: Named positions in the corpus's own vocabulary. Sides are given as -1/+1 multipliers on y, and ends as -1/+1 on x, so one entry serves both halves of the ice.

centre-point.$comment: The middle of the blue line — where a 1-3-1's single point player sets up. The name is a position name, not a claim that the point is the line: the same schematic caveat as `point` below applies, and for the same reasons.
centre-point.note: the middle of the blue line

point.$comment: SCHEMATIC ANCHOR — AND THIS NOTE USED TO STATE A RETRACTED DEFINITION. It read "at the blue line". content/foundation/rink_map_and_glossary.md denies that three times over: :356 "the point is the area just inside the blue line, not the line itself", :372 "'the point' is an *area*, not the blue line itself", :621 defines it as "the area just inside the blue line" once more, without the explicit contrast the other two carry — and :372 is a precision note written for exactly this confusion. x STAYS 25 ANYWAY, and the three reasons are not 'nobody got round to it'. (1) THE OWNER GIVES NO OFFSET, deliberately. The nearest it comes is "a little under 44 ft" from the half-wall (:683), and offensive_zone_play.md's instruction is behavioural — "stay a stride inside the line, not on it", because a puck completely crossing out clears the zone. Neither is a measurement. Picking an x > 25 would invent one. (2) THE OFFSET IS SMALLER THAN THE GLYPH THAT WOULD CARRY IT. SHAPE CARRIES THE POSITION AND FILL CARRIES THE TEAM, so this is about forwards and defencemen, not about sides: a FORWARD's circle is r 2.9, reaching 3.275 of ink with half its 0.75 stroke, and a DEFENCEMAN's triangle is 3.6 circumradius, reaching 4.0 with half its 0.8 round-joined stroke — either team, both figures read off the glyph branches in site/scripts/lib/rink.mjs. (An earlier version of this note read "an own-team circle ... and an opposition triangle 3.6 plus 0.8 of miter": the INVERTED notation axis this project has already adopted and reverted once, and wrong on the ink besides — the stroke contributes half its width, 0.4, and the join is round, not miter.) So at x 25 a circle already spans 22.1 to 27.9 and is half inside the line already. Drawing the player wholly inside it needs x of about 28 for a circle and 29 for a triangle — a number chosen to satisfy ink, not hockey, and larger than the hedge it would be claiming to draw. (3) BLAST RADIUS: this datum is anchored in over a hundred places across 11 diagram modules — `grep -oh "'point:[a-z:]*'" site/src/diagrams/*.mjs | wc -l` returned 101 on 2026-09-02 and 99 at that day's HEAD, and 14 further anchors reach the same x through `centre-point`. (This note used to say "109 times", which reproduces at neither, and a bare count copied into a comment goes stale the moment a diagram is written; re-run the grep rather than trusting the figure.) Twenty-six of the 101, in three modules — defending_the_rush.mjs, breakouts.mjs and faceoffs.mjs — use `point:*:far` purely as a NEUTRAL-ZONE landmark for the far blue line (e.g. `{ at: 'point:right:far', dx: -20, dy: 4 }  // (-45, 24)`), with the derived coordinate written into the comment beside it. Moving x would shift every one of those anchors and falsify the derived coordinate written into the comment beside each, for a correction that is about WORDS. See the half-wall note above: a datum restated in dozens of places is not a knob to turn. ⚠️ THE RETRACTION HAS LANDED — this paragraph used to say it was uncommitted and to cite line numbers that have all moved. Re-checked 2026-09-07: rink_map_and_glossary.md now denies the old definition at :371, :381, :385, :641, :707 and :777, the phrase "the point is at the blue line" appears NOWHERE in it, and :707's "44 ft" is hedged and explained ("a little under 44 ft", with the derivation given). ⚠️ NOTE WHAT WENT STALE AND HOW: not the geometry — the coordinate never moved and check_geometry still passes — but this note's account of ITS OWN STATUS, plus four line numbers, every one of which had shifted. A comment that tracks another file by line number goes stale silently the moment that file is edited above the line, and nothing in this repository checks it. The COORDINATE and every dimension check are unaffected either way: check_geometry's regexes were re-run against the HEAD text and all still match. SO: the marker is the blue-line end of the area; the CAPTIONS carry "just inside the line"; and scripts/check_geometry.py no longer asserts the retracted definition. If you think the coordinate should move, the thing to change first is the owner — get it to state a distance — not this file.
point.note: the blue-line end of the point; the point itself is the area just inside the line, not the line

half-wall.$comment: Was y=33 — 9.5 ft off the boards and INSIDE the faceoff circle, which reaches y=37 at this x. Four reviewers found players 'on the wall' standing in open ice, and two diagram authors had independently added per-diagram fudges rather than fixing it here. The owner says 'the boards roughly level with the faceoff dot', and this document's own schematic draws the half-wall hard against the side boards. 38.5 rather than 42.5 because a player standing against the wall does not have their centre ON the dasher. 40 was tried first and clipped every wall player by half a foot. ⚠️ DO NOT MOVE THIS TO FIX ONE GLYPH. It was briefly changed to 38.2 to stop a defenceman's triangle in breakout-reverse drawing through the boards — the apex reaches 3.6 ft from the centroid plus 0.4 of round-joined stroke, so 4.0, against an inner boards ink edge of 42.23 at THAT GLYPH's x of -73, which is on the corner arc, i.e. 0.27 ft over. (42.25 is the inner edge at the datum's own x of 69, on the straight boards; the two are different positions and this note first conflated them.) The move worked and cost far more than it fixed: this value is restated in comments across 10 diagram modules, six of which were not even being changed, and every one of them became false. (`grep -c "38\.5" site/src/diagrams/*.mjs` returned 59 lines on 2026-09-02, every one a comment; this note and breakouts.mjs both say 54, which is the figure at some earlier count and is not reproducible now. Re-run it rather than quoting it.) Exactly ONE glyph in the corpus is a triangle sitting on this datum with no dy — the other two half-wall triangles are 5 and 13 ft off it — so the fix belongs on that glyph, and it now carries dy -0.3 in breakouts.mjs. A datum restated in scores of places is not a knob to turn.
half-wall.note: the boards level with the faceoff dot

neutral-dot.$comment: Must equal faceoff.neutral_dot_x. It did not: the derived value was corrected to 20 and this named position was left at 30, so any diagram anchored here placed players 10 ft from the dot the same picture drew. check_geometry now asserts the two agree.

high-slot.note: dots to the top of the circles

slot.note: between the circles, in front of the net

goalmouth.$comment:
⚠️ THIS ANCHOR AND `net-front` BOTH SIT INSIDE THE BLUE PAINT, AND NEITHER NAME SAYS SO. On the centre line the crease reaches x = goal_line_x - crease_depth = 83, so goalmouth at 85 is 2 ft inside it and net-front at 84 is 1 ft inside. A forward's circle (r 2.9) centred on either is drawn squarely in the crease, and the corpus's own instruction is to keep skates off the red line, not merely out of the blue. The owner is looser than the coordinate: content/foundation/rink_map_and_glossary.md, §"The goalmouth", puts it "at the edge of the crease". NOT MOVED, and the words changed instead, for the usual reason: these name the mouth of the goal, which is where a puck and a scramble belong.

Every use of either datum was resolved by hand on 2026-09-02 — inline `pos: 'F'`/`pos: 'D'` glyphs, the `const` anchors (D_GOALMOUTH, BOX_LOW_R/L, both NET_FRONTs, D1_YOU) and the route endpoints — and every one carries a dx and/or dy that clears the crease ON THE MEASURE THAT AUDIT USED: a glyph's SOLID ink, body fill plus its own outline stroke (up to 3.275 ft from centre for a circle, up to 4.0 ft at a triangle's apex) — NOT the white halo drawn under every glyph, which is wider still. On that measure it holds: re-checked here, all five named anchors still clear on both bare fill and outlined body, D_GOALMOUTH the tightest at a claimed 0.04 ft of outlined-body daylight. ⚠️ THAT LAST FIGURE IS WRONG AND SO IS ITS SIGN. Re-derived 2026-09-07 by exact point-to-segment geometry AND by brute-force sampling of rink.mjs's own glyphCovers, agreeing to three decimals: at (83,-6) D_GOALMOUTH's BODY OVERLAPPED the crease by 0.028 ft — it never had daylight. The error came from measuring to the APEX: the triangle's nearest point to the crease is 15% down the apex-to-base edge, not the apex, and the naive apex measure gives 6.436 ft where the true distance is 6.372. The halo overlap was 0.628 ft — refuting BOTH a sweep that said 0.21 and a later re-derivation that said 0.939. FIXED: dy -6 -> -8, x unchanged, clearing crease halo by 0.418 ft. ⚠️ AND THAT MOVE WAS CONSTRAINED FROM THE OTHER SIDE by an overlap nobody had recorded: at (83,-6) the same glyph's halo already overlapped OPP_NETFRONT by 0.596 ft, so shifting dx to clear the crease — the fix the BACKDOOR/NET_FRONT precedent suggests — would have driven that to 1.479 ft. The two constraints pull opposite ways along x, which is why the fix is in y.

⚠️ IT DOES NOT HOLD ON THE HALO, which the 2026-09-02 audit's surviving working (preserved in special_teams.mjs's own comment on NET_FRONT) checked separately and accepted only when invisibly small. A corpus-wide sweep dated 2026-09-07, reading the renderer's own `loc()` and the exact triangle/circle paths `playSvg` draws, checked the halo everywhere for the first time and reported 8 of 797 skater glyphs corpus-wide with halo ink in the crease — the halo is real, opaque ink, 1.95 ft wide on a circle and 2.0 ft on a triangle, taking true reach to 3.875 ft uniform or 4.6 ft at a triangle's apex, not the body-stroke figures above. Two of the eight are tied to this file's own data. `D_GOALMOUTH` in `defensive_zone_coverage.mjs` (reused across four diagrams) was the other. ⚠️ THIS SENTENCE USED TO READ `dy:-6` … 'roughly 0.94 ft of halo — not a solid-body intrusion, still unresolved'. ALL THREE OF THOSE CLAIMS ARE NOW WRONG and they contradicted the paragraph above them in this same comment, which already recorded the fix. It is `dy:-8` at `defensive_zone_coverage.mjs:192`; the overlap at the old position was ~0.61–0.63 ft of halo (two independent re-derivations, differing only in metric definition) and NOT 0.94; and it DID include a solid-body intrusion of 0.028 ft. ⚠️ THE LESSON IS THE CONTRADICTION, NOT THE NUMBER: this one string carried a fixed state and an unresolved state simultaneously, each written by a different pass, each correct when written — the failure CLAUDE.md names as two agents writing individually-correct, flatly contradictory sentences into one block. It was caught by `commit-gate` reading the whole string instead of the paragraph it had changed. `special_teams.mjs`'s `BACKDOOR` (`pp-backdoor`'s `BD`) was worse, and outside the five anchors the 2026-09-02 audit named: it overlapped by roughly 0.96 ft of halo AND 0.36 ft of its own solid outline stroke, because its dx (-3) did not actually match the dx (-4) its own comment claimed to mirror from NET_FRONT — the mirror claim was false, not just the clearance. Fixed on 2026-09-07 to dx -4 (see that file's own comment on `BACKDOOR`), which inherits NET_FRONT's own already-accepted 0.05 ft (half-a-pixel, invisible) halo-only overlap instead of a visible one.

USE A dy: an unoffset skater on either datum is a diagram of a player in the crease. `check_geometry` does not assert either measure, deliberately — an assertion that these datums clear the crease on the halo measure held only after the 2026-09-07 fixes; before them it would have failed, and treating the solid-body measure as the whole story is exactly the gap this note is now correcting. Re-derive rather than trust this note: `grep -n "'net-front'\|'goalmouth'" site/src/diagrams/*.mjs`, and remember the crease front is a curved arc, not a straight line at x = 83 — the nearest boundary point to an off-centre anchor is usually on that arc, closer than a quick |y| <= 4 read suggests.
goalmouth.note: immediate net front, and 2 ft inside the crease — see $comment

net-front.note: 1 ft inside the crease on the centre line — see the goalmouth $comment; offset any skater drawn here

bumper.note: the middle player of a 1-3-1 — a role, not a fixed spot
